key_insight: A purely physics-driven P-PINN framework can learn parametric periodic unsteady flows directly and use them to predict finite-amplitude aeroelastic responses without long transient CFD time marching.
engineering_relevance: This enables fast, reusable aeroelastic response prediction across operating and structural parameters, cutting repeated high-fidelity simulation costs from hours or days to seconds after training.
method: Impose temporal periodicity over one motion cycle in a Periodic Physics-Informed Neural Network (P-PINN).
Include flow conditions and motion parameters as inputs to build continuous parametric maps of periodic flow fields and aerodynamic forces.
Couple the parametric aerodynamic model with a single-degree-of-freedom structural equation via first-order harmonic balance to solve response amplitude and frequency.
evidence_signal: The framework is validated on forced-motion circular cylinder and airfoil cases and on an elastically mounted circular cylinder, with results matching time-marching and fully coupled CFD/CSD responses for forces, loads, flow fields, and aeroelastic response curves.
watch_item: Accuracy depends on the network’s ability to represent periodic states and may be sensitive to training coverage across Reynolds numbers, motion amplitudes, and structural parameter ranges.
paper_title: A Physics-Driven Framework for Parametric Periodic-Flow Modeling and Finite-Amplitude Aeroelastic Response Analysis
